canonical_record.label: SH0ES baseline Cepheid-SN H0 result
canonical_record.summary: The SH0ES analysis reports a baseline Cepheid-SN H0 result of 73.04+-1.04 km/s/Mpc, including systematics.

sources.title: A Comprehensive Measurement of the Local Value of the Hubble Constant with 1 km/s/Mpc Uncertainty from the Hubble Space Telescope and the SH0ES Team

assertions.statement: The SH0ES analysis reports a baseline Cepheid-SN H0 result of 73.04+-1.04 km/s/Mpc, including systematics.

scope.population: The Cepheid-SN sample analyzed by SH0ES.

support.quote: Our baseline result from the Cepheid-SN sample is H0=73.04+-1.04 km/s/Mpc, which includes systematics and lies near the median of all analysis variants.

decisions.rationale: The retained SH0ES source exactly states: 'Our baseline result from the Cepheid-SN sample is H0=73.04+-1.04 km/s/Mpc, which includes systematics and lies near the median of all analysis variants.' The candidate summary preserves that result as an attributed report, retains the Cepheid-SN sample scope, the numerical value and units, and the inclusion of systematics without adding a consensus, truth, replication, or current-frontier claim. Kind=claim is appropriate for a reported quantitative result in the source; domain=physical is justified by the cosmological H0 measurement. Under the supplied representation_policy, status=reported asserts only source attribution, era=undated leaves chronology unresolved, and frontier=false makes no positive currency claim, so those neutral fields do not strengthen the scientific content. No edge, identity, taxonomy placement, or directional relationship is asserted.
decisions.limitations: Support is limited to the SH0ES team's reported baseline Cepheid-SN H0 result and its stated inclusion of systematics. This decision does not establish that the value is scientifically accepted, independently replicated, currently preferred, a present frontier result, or correct beyond the attributed source. The candidate also does not encode the source's additional statement that the value lies near the median of its analysis variants; omission of that extra detail does not strengthen the retained claim.

decisions.rationale: The retained SH0ES source directly and exactly supports the candidate's substantive statement. Its abstract states: 'Our baseline result from the Cepheid-SN sample is H0=73.04+-1.04 km/s/Mpc, which includes systematics and lies near the median of all analysis variants.' support.quote:
Title:
A Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity

Here, we introduce an idea for such a test based on the principle that two objects cannot be entangled without a quantum mediator. We show that despite the weakness of gravity, the phase evolution induced by the gravitational interaction of two micron size test masses in adjacent matter-wave interferometers can detectably entangle them even when they are placed far apart enough to keep Casimir-Polder forces at bay. We provide a prescription for witnessing this entanglement, which certifies gravity as a quantum coherent mediator, through simple correlation measurements between two spins: one embedded in each test mass.

Subjects:
Quantum Physics (quant-ph)
; General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology (gr-qc); High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

support.quote:
Title:
Dark Matter Search Results from 4.2 Tonne-Years of Exposure of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) Experiment

We report results of a search for nuclear recoils induced by weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter using the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) two-phase xenon time projection chamber. This analysis uses a total exposure of $4.2\pm0.1$ tonne-years from 280 live days of LZ operation, of which $3.3\pm0.1$ tonne-years and 220 live days are new.
After removal of artificial signal-like events injected into the data set to mitigate analyzer bias, we find no evidence for an excess over expected backgrounds.
